legal.disclaimer: These terms and this privacy policy apply to AcrossFlare, operated by 어크로스툴 (CEO: 신일) at acrossflare.com.

termsSections.title: 1. Parties
termsSections.body: These terms govern the secure-cloud and network-optimization digital service AcrossFlare, provided by 어크로스툴 (“the company”). You accept them when you sign up or pay.

termsSections.title: 2. The service
termsSections.body:
Paid products listed on the site are Standard, Hybrid, and Workspace & Custom. Each includes encrypted network access and encrypted cloud backup. Routes (such as LA or Tokyo+LA), traffic, backup size, term, and seat counts follow the product page and checkout screen.

After payment succeeds or the company provisions an account manually, access and backup details are issued to the signed-in account. Workspace plans require a promotional code. The catalog on the homepage may change.

termsSections.title: 3. Accounts
termsSections.body: You must be 14 or older. Provide an accurate email and keep your password secret. You are responsible for issued access and backup credentials. After sign-in you can view your email in Settings. To change the email or delete the account, email acrosstool@gmail.com.

termsSections.title: 4. Acceptable use
termsSections.body: Use the service only for lawful purposes such as travel, work trips, and online meetings. You must not use it to attack networks, commit fraud, distribute malware, exploit minors, evade legal duties, or violate export or sanctions rules. The company may restrict or end service for abuse, non-payment, or legal need.

termsSections.title: 5. Payments and plans
termsSections.body:
Prices include VAT and are shown in the currency that follows your language. Card and Alipay charges are processed by PortOne, Stripe, or Paymentwall. All paid plans are one-time purchases only; we do not offer recurring billing, auto-renewal, or automatic card charges. When your term ends, you must pay again to extend access.

For Standard and Hybrid, digital delivery (access and backup details) starts immediately when payment succeeds. For Workspace, you pay after a promotional code is confirmed, and the company issues details to the account. Traffic, backup quota, and term follow the plan; unused traffic does not roll over unless stated. Withdrawals and refunds follow section 6.

termsSections.title: 6. Withdrawals and refunds
termsSections.body:
This is digital content whose supply starts when payment succeeds. After access or backup details are issued, the right to withdraw may be limited under Korean e-commerce law (Article 17(2)(5)). We disclose that on the payment screen and require your agreement.

Email acrosstool@gmail.com within 7 days of payment for a full refund if (1) payment succeeded but access or backup details were not issued or provisioning failed, or (2) the charge was duplicated or clearly erroneous.

We do not pro-rate unused time after details have been issued, unless a mandatory law says otherwise.

Refunds go back to the original payment method. By statute a refund should begin within three business days of the withdrawal request; the payment provider may take several more days to post it. Purchase-protection (escrow) is not offered for this digital content.

termsSections.title: 7. Availability
termsSections.body: Network routes, access systems, and backup storage may move, fail over, be maintained, or go offline. We work to keep the service available but do not warrant uninterrupted access or a particular exit IP.

termsSections.title: 8. Termination
termsSections.body: You may stop using the service at any time. The company may end a contract for non-payment, breach, or legal need. Access and backup may be revoked without a separate notice period.

termsSections.title: 9. Liability
termsSections.body: The service is provided as available. To the extent allowed by law, the company is not liable for lost profits, lost data, or indirect damages, and total liability for a claim is limited to the fees paid for the affected subscription in the prior three months.

termsSections.title: 10. Governing law
termsSections.body: These terms follow the laws of the Republic of Korea. Disputes follow Korean e-commerce and consumer rules; you may also use Korea Consumer Agency procedures. Contact: acrosstool@gmail.com, phone 070-8065-1258.

termsSections.title: 11. Changes
termsSections.body: We may update these terms on this page. Changes that are unfavorable to you will be announced before they apply. Continued use after a posted change means you accept the new terms.

privacySections.title: 1. Purpose and data we collect
privacySections.body: We process personal data to register accounts, provide the paid service, handle payment and refunds, answer support, and protect against abuse. We store email, password hashes, session cookies, plan and payment records, issued access and backup details, and operational logs. For card checkout we also collect a mobile phone number so the payment processor can verify the payer. We do not store card numbers; payment processors do.

privacySections.title: 2. Retention
privacySections.body: Account data is kept until you leave or the contract ends. Transaction records are kept for the periods required by Korean e-commerce and tax rules (generally five years for contracts, payments, and supply records, and three years for complaint records). Session cookies expire. Issued secrets are removed or rotated when a plan changes or ends; backup copies may remain for a limited time.

privacySections.title: 3. Processors
privacySections.body:
We outsource personal-data processing as follows.

Processor: PortOne Co., Ltd. (주식회사 포트원) — payments (electronic payment gateway)
Processor: Stripe, Inc. — payments (including Alipay)
Processor: Paymentwall, Inc. — payments
Processor: Cloudflare, Inc. — website hosting, DNS, WAF, and TLS
Processor: VPS providers used to run servers — server hosting

Retention lasts until the processing contract ends, or as required by law under section 2. Encrypted backup features use our password, note, and file-sync systems. We do not sell personal information.

privacySections.title: 4. Overseas transfers
privacySections.body: Data may be transferred abroad to run the service: Cloudflare (United States and other regions, DNS and security), Stripe and Paymentwall (United States and other regions, payments), and overseas VPS providers (including the United States and Japan, servers). Items may include email, payment identifiers, and technical access data. Retention follows section 2. Signing up or paying with this policy in view is how we inform you of those transfers.

privacySections.title: 5. Sharing with third parties
privacySections.body: We do not provide personal data to third parties except where the law requires it.

privacySections.title: 6. Deletion and security
privacySections.body: When the retention period ends we destroy personal data so it cannot be restored. We use access control, TLS, password hashing, and permission limits.

privacySections.title: 7. Your rights
privacySections.body: After sign-in you can view your account email in Settings. To change the email, access or correct data, pause processing, or delete the account, email acrosstool@gmail.com unless we must keep records for law or security. Do not send payment card numbers to that inbox.

privacySections.title: 8. Children under 14
privacySections.body: We do not collect personal data from children under 14. They may not create an account.

privacySections.title: 9. Cookies
privacySections.body: We use session cookies to keep you signed in and to protect the account. Blocking cookies may disable sign-in.

privacySections.title: 10. Privacy officer
privacySections.body: Privacy officer: 신일. Email acrosstool@gmail.com, phone 070-8065-1258.

privacySections.title: 11. Remedies
privacySections.body: You may contact the Personal Information Infringement Report Center (privacy.kisa.or.kr / 118), the Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee (www.kopico.go.kr / 1833-6972), the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office cyber investigation unit (www.spo.go.kr / 1301), or the National Police Agency cyber investigation unit (ecrm.police.go.kr / 182).

privacySections.title: 12. Changes
privacySections.body: We post updates on this page and announce material changes before they apply.

downloads.title: Download Center
downloads.lead: Use the button below to install the latest client for this device.

install.windows: Run the .exe installer. If SmartScreen appears, choose More info → Run anyway.
install.macos: Open the .dmg and drag Karing to Applications. If macOS warns about an unidentified developer, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.
install.android: Open the APK and allow installs from this source if asked. Karing is not on the Play Store.
install.ios: Install Karing from the App Store. Do not use unofficial IPA files.
install.linux: Make the AppImage executable, then run it.

install.title: Run the Karing installer
install.body: Open the downloaded file and follow the installer. Use the OS notes below for your device.

profile.title: Add the issued QR code or subscription link
profile.body: After payment, click Console in the top right of the screen. Your QR code and connection link are generated there. Scan that QR in Karing, or copy the URL and paste it into Add Profile. You can also copy the QR image.

connect.title: Connect
connect.body: After the profile is saved, turn on the main switch to connect. Open backup from the profile webpage or the announcement “Open backup space”.

backup.title: How to use backup
backup.heading: Keep passwords and small files in the browser. You do not need a separate backup app.

open.title: Open vault / Open sync
open.body: In Console or Backup, open Vaultwarden (password & note backup) with Open vault, and Syncthing (small file storage) with Open sync. Both open in the browser.

save.title: Save passwords, notes, and small files
save.body: Store passwords and notes in Vaultwarden, and small files in your Syncthing folder.

optional.title: Optional device folder sync
optional.body: To keep a phone or PC folder in sync automatically, install Syncthing on that device and connect it with the folder ID on screen. Skip that if you only upload and download small files in the browser.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.helpBody: If you need remote help or a 1:1 walkthrough, contact the support team.

profileWhere.q: Where do I get the subscription QR code or link?
profileWhere.a: After payment, click Console in the top right of the screen. Your QR code and connection link are generated there. Scan that QR in Karing, or copy the URL and paste it into Add Profile. You can also copy the QR image.

playStore.q: Can I get Android from the Play Store?
playStore.a: Karing is not on the Play Store. Use the download button on this page or the official GitHub Releases APK.

macOpen.q: macOS says the developer cannot be verified.
macOpen.a: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.

manualRefresh.q: What should I do after a traffic limit notice or when nodes disappear?
manualRefresh.a: The server refreshes usage about every 5 minutes, but Karing may auto-fetch the subscription only once every 24 hours. If you see a traffic limit notice or nodes are missing, tap Manual subscription update at the top of the Karing app.

backupApp.q: Do I have to install an app to use backup?
backupApp.a: No. Use Vaultwarden (password & note backup) and Syncthing (small file storage) in the browser. Only network access needs the Karing app.

backupFromKaring.q: How do I open backup from Karing?
backupFromKaring.a: After you add the subscription, tap the profile webpage or the “Open backup space” announcement. It opens backup in the browser. You will need to sign in to AcrossFlare once.

vaultLogin.q: How do I sign in to Vaultwarden?
vaultLogin.a: Open vault from Backup, then use the issued vault address and your account email.

deviceSync.q: How do I keep files on my phone in sync?
deviceSync.a: Install Syncthing on that device and connect it with the folder ID on screen. You do not need that if you only upload and download small files in the browser.
